findings.trigger: A channel has 'control' permission; a user opens the info panel and receives ContainerInfoAdminView (built by StatusInfoButton.callback:950). The operator then revokes 'control' on that channel while the view is still alive (it lives up to 890s). Within that window the same user presses 'Edit Info' (EditInfoButton.callback:271) or 'Debug Logs' (DebugLogsButton.callback:718) -> both callbacks run straight to opening the edit modal / fetching live logs with no permission check of any kind (no _channel_has_permission, no _admin_may_control), so the now-unauthorized user can still rewrite the container's info text/address settings or read its live logs. Contrast: ProtectedInfoEditButton.callback (same file, lines 217-229) explicitly re-checks '_channel_has_permission(...) or _admin_may_control(...)' at press time for exactly this reason (its own comment cites 'review F3'), but EditInfoButton and DebugLogsButton never got the same recheck even though they sit in the identical ContainerInfoAdminView and were built by the identical (potentially stale) gate.
findings.suggestion: Add the same current-permission recheck used in ProtectedInfoEditButton.callback ('_channel_has_permission(interaction.channel_id, 'control', config) or _admin_may_control(interaction.user.id, self.container_name)') to EditInfoButton.callback and DebugLogsButton.callback before they act, matching the operator's 2026-09-16 decision that a channel losing 'control' must make open admin panels lose their effect immediately.

findings.trigger: A user is on the (global or container-scoped) admin list but presses the info button (StatusInfoButton.callback) in a channel that has only 'status', not 'control', permission. 'has_control' at line 929 is computed purely from '_channel_has_permission(interaction.channel_id, 'control', config)'; it never calls '_admin_may_control'. Since has_control is False, 'view' stays None (lines 946-951) and the admin gets the plain info embed with no ContainerInfoAdminView at all - no Edit Info, no Protected Info Edit, no Debug Logs, no Task Management - even though the same file's ProtectedInfoEditButton.callback shows the '_admin_may_control' mechanism exists precisely to let an admin act 'where the channel alone permits nothing (the status channels)' (SPEC.md Z5/B2).
findings.suggestion: If admins are meant to reach the info-admin buttons from status-only channels (per B2), OR '_admin_may_control(interaction.user.id, self.container_name)' into the 'has_control' computation at line 929 the same way ProtectedInfoEditButton.callback already does at press time.
findings.unsure_why: ContainerInfoAdminView's own docstring (line 109) says it is for 'control channels only', which may mean this specific admin-edit surface is deliberately out of B2's scope rather than a gap. I also cannot see control_helpers.py (not in the provided source), so I cannot rule out that '_channel_has_permission' itself already folds in admin-list membership, which would make the explicit 'or _admin_may_control(...)' in ProtectedInfoEditButton redundant defense-in-depth rather than evidence of a missing check elsewhere.

findings.trigger: ContainerInfoAdminView is constructed at line 950 as 'ContainerInfoAdminView(self.cog, self.server_config, self.info_config)' with no 'message=' argument, so 'self.message' stays None (the __init__ default). After sending it via 'interaction.followup.send(embed=embed, view=view, ephemeral=True)' (line 955), the returned message object is never written back to 'view.message' - unlike the sibling LiveLogView in the same file, where DebugLogsButton.callback explicitly sets 'view.message_ref = message' (line 814) or passes it into 'start_auto_refresh(message)' (line 811), which stores it at line 475. Because 'self.message' is always None for this view, 'on_timeout' (lines 134-152) never enters its 'if self.message:' deletion branch, and 'start_auto_delete_timer' (lines 153-171) - which is also never scheduled from __init__ or anywhere else in this file - would be a no-op even if it ran. The stale ephemeral admin panel is therefore never cleaned up when its 890-second view timeout fires.
findings.suggestion: Pass the sent message back into the view, e.g. 'view.message = message' right after 'interaction.followup.send(...)' in StatusInfoButton.callback (mirroring how DebugLogsButton.callback wires up LiveLogView.message_ref), and either call 'start_auto_delete_timer()' as a background task from ContainerInfoAdminView.__init__ or remove the unused method if on_timeout alone is meant to cover cleanup.

findings.trigger: In LiveLogView.toggle_updates' 'currently stopped - START' branch (lines 633-667), 'self.auto_refresh_enabled = True' is set at line 637, before the message edit and before the new refresh task is created at line 660 inside the try block. If 'self.message_ref.edit(...)' raises HTTPException/NotFound (line 654, caught at 663-664 and only logged at DEBUG), execution never reaches 'asyncio.create_task(self._auto_refresh_loop())', so no refresh task is actually running - yet 'self.auto_refresh_enabled' stays True and 'self.auto_refresh_task' still holds the previous (already cancelled) task object from the last STOP, which is truthy. The next time the same button is pressed, 'if self.auto_refresh_enabled and self.auto_refresh_task:' (line 608) evaluates True, so the code takes the STOP path (cancelling an already-cancelled task) instead of retrying START - the view's internal state silently disagrees with what is actually running, with no error shown to the user beyond a transient '⏳ Updating...' message.
findings.suggestion: Only set 'self.auto_refresh_enabled = True' and create the new task after the message edit succeeds (or reset 'self.auto_refresh_enabled = False' and clear 'self.auto_refresh_task' in the except branch), so a failed edit cannot leave the enabled flag and the task object out of sync.

notes: Several names referenced from this file (TaskManagementButton, DeleteTasksButton, ContainerTaskDeleteButton, control_helpers._channel_has_permission/_admin_may_control, enhanced_info_modal_simple modals, container_info_service, game_query_service) live in files not included in this section's source/ (only cogs/status_info_integration.py, cogs/info_extras.py and cogs/player_joins.py were provided), so their internal behaviour was not verified and F2's severity in particular depends on code I could not see. should_show_info_in_status_channel (cogs/status_info_integration.py:1107) computes 'has_control' via _channel_has_permission but never uses it, unconditionally returning True; its own comment says this is deliberate ('For now, show info integration in all status channels'), so I did not report the unused variable as a finding, only noting it here. cogs/info_extras.py and cogs/player_joins.py were read in full and no defects were found beyond what is already documented in SPEC.md as fixed (e.g. the 2026-09-28 address/port ordering and the Enshrouded stale-status fix).
